post_title: Why Our Jack Russell Barks at the Fence (and Why We Let Him)

meta.rank_math_title: Jack Russell Terrier Barking: Why Ours Barks & When It Stops
meta.rank_math_description: Tery, our 5-month-old Jack Russell, barks at people walking past the fence, never at nothing. What sets him off, what we do, and when barking is a problem.

thedoghabit_faq.question: Why does my Jack Russell bark at people walking past?
thedoghabit_faq.answer: Jack Russells are alert, territorial working terriers, and barking at someone near the boundary is a way of guarding the house. Our Jack Russell barks at people walking past our outer fence even though he cannot see through it, so he reacts to what he hears. He stops once the person has gone.

thedoghabit_faq.question: Should I stop my Jack Russell from barking at the fence?
thedoghabit_faq.answer: It depends on whether the barking ends. If your dog barks at a real trigger and stops once it is gone, it is normal guarding. We let our terrier bark, call him once the passer-by has gone, and reward him when he comes back. Barking that never ends, starts suddenly, or comes with signs of fear or pain is worth a closer look.

thedoghabit_faq.question: Why does my Jack Russell bark at thunder and wind?
thedoghabit_faq.answer: Thunder and strong wind are loud, sudden noises, and an alert terrier will often bark at them. Our Jack Russell barks at both. If your dog also trembles, hides, pants or tries to escape during storms, the barking may be fear rather than alerting, and a safe, quiet place helps more than a command.

thedoghabit_faq.question: Do Jack Russell Terriers bark a lot?
thedoghabit_faq.answer: They are a vocal breed and they notice everything, so they bark more readily than many dogs. In our experience it is not random: our Jack Russell barks at passers-by, the doorbell, loud sounds outside, thunder and wind, and never at nothing.
